title: Tooltips show their keyboard shortcuts, and menus and hints show the platform's usual key (⌘⌫, ⌘[ on macOS)
problem: No control's tooltip names its shortcut, though each has one: Back and Forward (src/finder/toolbar.rs:317-330; bound at src/actions.rs:137-140), the four view buttons (toolbar.rs:333-343; actions.rs:148-151), Show and Hide Sidebar (toolbar.rs:509-510; src/finder/sidebar.rs:475-476; actions.rs:156), Close Tab (src/finder/tab_bar.rs:349-352; actions.rs:129), Filter with Nushell and Search Syntax (src/finder/bars.rs:130-133, 150-153; actions.rs:167-168). The tab bar's + button has no tooltip at all (tab_bar.rs:416-426). The shortcuts appear only in the macOS menu bar; Linux and Windows have no menu bar and the Actions menu (toolbar.rs:708-828) doesn't list these commands, so nothing in the window teaches them. The kit supports this already: `Button::tooltip_with_action` (gpui-component-0.8.1/src/button/button.rs:430) and `Tooltip::action` (tooltip.rs:74). Separately, menus show an action's last-registered binding (gpui-fast-0.1.12/src/key_dispatch.rs:374-387, `.rev().find`). actions.rs:141-143 knows this and orders Enclosing Folder for it. But Move to Trash registers `secondary-backspace` and then `delete` (actions.rs:222, 226; 242-243 for the tree), and Back/Forward register `secondary-[`/`]` and then `alt-left`/`alt-right` (137-140). So on macOS the item menu, the Actions menu and File › Move to Trash show ⌦, a key MacBook keyboards lack, and Go › Back/Forward show ⌥←/⌥→ where Finder shows ⌘[/⌘]; the new tooltip hints would show the same.
proposal: (a) Replace `.tooltip(text)` with `.tooltip_with_action(text, &Action, Some(FINDER))` on back, forward, view-icons/list/columns/gallery (pass the matching action into `view_button`), show-sidebar and hide-sidebar. For the hand-built tooltips use `Tooltip::new(text).action(&ToggleFilter, Some(FINDER))` (and SearchHelp; CloseWindow for Close Tab). Give `new-tab` a 'New Tab' tooltip with `NewTab`. (b) In `bind_keys` (actions.rs:119-267) order those pairs by platform through a small helper, so the last one registered is the platform's usual key: on macOS `delete` before `secondary-backspace` (files and tree) and `alt-left`/`alt-right` before `secondary-[`/`secondary-]`; elsewhere as now, where Delete and Alt+Left are the convention. No key stops working; only what menus and tooltips display changes.
original_test_plan: Unit tests in src/actions.rs: a pure `menu_order(mac_usual, other_usual, is_macos)` helper checked for both values (runs on Linux), plus a `#[gpui_kit::test]` that calls `bind_keys` and asserts the keymap's last binding for `MoveToTrash` and `GoBack` is `delete`/`alt-left` off macOS and `cmd-backspace`/`cmd-[` on it via `cfg!`. Headless UI test in tests/controls.rs: for each (action, Finder) pair the tooltips use, `ui.window(|w, _| Kbd::binding_for_action(&action, Some("Finder"), w).is_some())`; then `ui.hover("new-tab")` and `ui.hover("view-list")` and assert a tooltip appears (the kit's tooltip element is `tooltip-popup`, tooltip.rs:115). Check that Alt+Left and Cmd+[ both still go back.
original_risks: The macOS half of (b) cannot be seen on Linux; the test only pins the ordering rule. The second reviewer proposed moving Alt+Left/Right above Cmd+[/] on every platform, which would make Linux and Windows hints read Ctrl+[ instead of the conventional Alt+Left; the platform-aware helper is used here instead. In `--term` mode the Ctrl aliases are bound last (actions.rs:249-258) and will be what tooltips show, as menus already do. Tooltips get slightly wider; check the key hint's look in light and dark. Shares toolbar.rs with the split-view-toolbar-clip and history-menus candidates.

verifier.claim_check:
REG = /root/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f

Part (a), tooltips: true for the main window.
- Plain `.tooltip(text)`: src/finder/toolbar.rs:318, 326, 339, 510 and src/finder/sidebar.rs:476.
- `Tooltip::new(..)` with no action: src/finder/tab_bar.rs:349-352 and src/finder/bars.rs:130-133, 150-153.
- `new-tab` has no tooltip (tab_bar.rs:416-426).
- All eight actions are bound in the `Finder` context (src/actions.rs:129-130, 137-140, 148-151, 156, 167-168), and `Button::tooltip_with_action` and `Tooltip::action` exist (REG/gpui-component-0.8.1/src/button/button.rs:430, tooltip.rs:74).
- Two overstatements. Quick Look and the PDF toolbar already name shortcuts this way (src/finder/explore.rs:965, 971; preview.rs:689; pdf.rs:766). The Actions menu does carry New Tab, Filter with Nushell… and Search Syntax… as actions, so with key hints (toolbar.rs:722-725, 808-810, 818).

Part (b), binding order: the premise is false for the macOS menu bar.
- The app builds on gpui-pre 0.3.10, not the cited gpui-fast (only gpui-pre-* is in target/debug/.fingerprint).
- Kit popup menus and tooltips do show the last matching binding (REG/gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/key_dispatch.rs:420-433; REG/gpui-component-0.8.1/src/menu/popup_menu.rs:1138-1164).
- The macOS menu bar does not. `create_menu_item` uses `keymap.bindings_for_action(..).find_or_first(..)` against Zed's Workspace/Pane/Editor context (gpui-pre-macos-0.3.10/src/platform.rs:342-366). That crate is not in the local registry on Linux; I fetched the published source to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fffinder/77fc8bed-98cd-53c5-aa96-589871b38301/scratchpad/macos-src/gpui-pre-macos-0.3.10/src/platform.rs. fffinder's contexts never match, so the menu bar shows the first binding registered.
- So File › Move to Trash already shows ⌘⌫ (actions.rs:222 comes before 226), and Go › Back/Forward already show ⌘[ and ⌘] (137-138 before 139-140).
- The comment at actions.rs:141 has the rule backwards for the menu bar: with alt-up first, Go › Enclosing Folder shows ⌥↑.

What is actually wrong on macOS is the kit menus. Move to Trash in the item menu (src/finder/menus.rs:331) and the Actions menu (toolbar.rs:785-788) takes `delete`, which the kit draws as a bare ⌫ (REG/gpui-component-0.8.1/src/kbd.rs:173-174), not ⌦. Linux and Windows are right today.

None of the macOS behaviour was run; it is from reading the platform code.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Do (a) with three corrections, and replace (b).

(a) Tooltips
1. toolbar.rs:318, 326: `.tooltip_with_action("Back", &GoBack, Some(FINDER))`, and the same for Forward. toolbar.rs:333-343: add an `action: &dyn Action` parameter to `view_button` (ViewIcons, ViewList, ViewColumns, ViewGallery). toolbar.rs:510 and sidebar.rs:476: `&ToggleSidebar`. Kit `Button` has no public tooltip builder and is not a `StatefulInteractiveElement` (button.rs:224, 614), so this is the only route and it always shows the last binding.
2. bars.rs:130-133 and 150-153, tab_bar.rs:349-352, and a new tooltip on `new-tab` (before `.test_support()` at tab_bar.rs:425): add `.action(.., Some(FINDER))` with ToggleFilter, SearchHelp, CloseWindow and NewTab. Build these four through one helper, for example `pub(super) fn shortcut_tooltip(label, action)` in toolbar.rs. It should use `Tooltip::element` with a child `div().id("shortcut-tip").aria_label(label).test_support()`, as fit.rs:59-68 does for `cut-off-text`. That is what makes them testable.
3. Close Tab: show the CloseWindow key only on the active tab (`on`, tab_bar.rs:313). Cmd+W closes the active tab (tab_bar.rs:199-217), not the one under the pointer.
4. Optional, same pattern: nu_panel.rs:100 hard-codes "Close (Ctrl-`)"; `tooltip_with_action("Close", &ToggleNuPanel, Some(FINDER))` would match the rest.

(b) Binding order in actions.rs
- Do not register the Mac key last only, which is what the proposed `menu_order` does. The macOS menu bar would then show ⌦ for Move to Trash and ⌥←/⌥→ for Back and Forward, the very state the candidate describes as the bug.
- Factor the table into `fn key_table(mac: bool, cx: &App) -> Vec<KeyBinding>`; `bind_keys` passes `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`.
- On macOS put Finder's key at both ends. Keep it first (menu bar) and append it again after the table, before the `--term` aliases are derived (249-256): `secondary-[` GoBack, `secondary-]` GoForward, `secondary-up` GoUp (finder context), `secondary-backspace` MoveToTrash (files and tree). This is right whichever end a consumer reads, so kit menus show ⌘⌫ and the Back/Forward tooltips show ⌘[ and ⌘].
- The repeat is safe: dispatch stops at the first handled binding (REG/gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/window.rs:6196-6208), and these handlers never call `cx.propagate()` (only pdf.rs:611 does).
- Swap 142-143 so `secondary-up` comes first, and correct the comment at 141 (menu bar: first binding; kit menus and tooltips: last).
- Leave the Linux and Windows order as it is; Delete and Alt+Left are already last.

Docs: add an Unreleased line to CHANGELOG.md and a sentence to the Toolbar section of docs/manual.md (164-186).
verifier.test_plan:
Unit test in src/actions.rs, beside the two existing `#[gpui_kit::test]` tests (same `cx.update`, `key()`, `context()`, `binding.keystrokes()[0].inner()` helpers):
- Call `key_table(true, cx)` and `key_table(false, cx)` and compare keystrokes with `key("secondary-[", ..)` and friends. On Linux `secondary` is Ctrl, so both orderings run there.
- With `mac`: the first binding of GoBack, GoForward, GoUp and MoveToTrash is the `secondary` one, and so is the last one per context.
- Without: the last GoBack is `alt-left` and the last MoveToTrash per context is `delete`.

Headless UI test in tests/controls.rs, using `Ui` from tests/common/mod.rs:
- For GoBack, GoForward, the four view actions, ToggleSidebar, NewTab, CloseWindow, ToggleFilter and SearchHelp, assert `ui.window(|window, _| Kbd::binding_for_action(&action, Some(FINDER), window).is_some())`.
- For GoBack, check the key itself through `window.highest_precedence_binding_for_action_in_context(&GoBack, KeyContext::parse(FINDER).unwrap())`: alt-left off macOS, cmd-[ on it via `cfg!`.
- Hover: the proposed `tooltip-popup` check cannot work. The kit never registers that element (REG/gpui-base-0.8.1/src/tooltip.rs:28-31), and the harness only finds `.test_support()` elements (REG/gpui-base-0.8.1/src/test_support.rs:209-242).
- Instead open with `Open { workspace: true, .. }`, `ui.press(&cmd("t"))` to get the tab bar, `ui.hover("new-tab")`, then assert `ui.snapshot("shortcut-tip").label() == Some("New Tab")`. Do the same for `("close-tab", 1usize)`, and for `filter-toggle` and `search-help` after `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query("atlas".into(), true, cx))`. Put `ui.hover_point(at(0., 0.))` between hovers, as tests/columns.rs does.
- `ui.hover("back")` and `ui.hover("view-list")` are smoke checks only; kit Button tooltips expose nothing to the harness.
- Press `delete` on a selected file and `alt-up` in a subfolder. No existing test presses either, and the table is being refactored.

Already covered: Cmd+[ and ], Alt+Left and Right, and Cmd+Up in tests/finder.rs:25-37; Cmd+Backspace in tests/basics.rs:1115 and tests/file_ops.rs:667.
verifier.risks:
- The macOS outcome cannot be run on Linux; it rests on reading gpui-pre-macos. Check once on a Mac: the Go menu shows ⌘[ ⌘] ⌘↑, File › Move to Trash shows ⌘⌫, the item menu's Move to Trash shows ⌘⌫, and the Back tooltip shows ⌘[.
- The repeated macOS bindings would run a handler twice if one of those handlers ever starts calling `cx.propagate()`.
- In `--term` on macOS the Ctrl aliases stay last, so hints show the Ctrl form, as docs/manual.md:761 says menus do. The repeats must be added before the aliases are derived to keep that.
- Not covered here: by the same first-binding rule, the macOS menu bar shows F5 for View › Refresh (actions.rs:154 comes before 155).
- Tooltips get slightly wider; check the key hint in light and dark.
- toolbar.rs is shared with the split-view-toolbar-clip and history-menus candidates.
